- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate in the final 5–10 days of the forecast; adjust upward slightly to account for mean reversion or tail risk.
- When true values show strong upward momentum, model tends to overreact and overshoot; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% above recent high.
- If history shows persistent downward trend, model often fails to recognize it; apply slight downward bias in forecast mean.
- Forecast tends to lag true values by 1–3 days; adjust for lag by shifting forecast values forward by 1–2 days in the next update.
- Avoid overfitting to recent volatility; if last 5 days show high variance, reduce forecast sensitivity to short-term noise.
